meanings.note: Russian imperfective verb expressing ongoing, habitual, or repeated action meaning 'to be'; conjugates for person and number in the present/future and agrees in gender in the past tense.

examples.text: Расслабься, друг, время ещё есть.
examples.trans: Relax, friend, there is still time.

examples.text: В следующий раз нож будет выше!
examples.trans: Next time the knife will be higher!

examples.text: Нельзя же быть такой злой утром!
examples.trans: One must not be so mean in the morning!

meanings.note: Invariable Russian adverb used to modify verbs or whole clauses with the sense 'how'.

examples.text: Как он появился, сразу стали пропадать продукты!
examples.trans: As soon as he appeared, groceries immediately started disappearing!

examples.text: О, вот как раз Дима звонит!
examples.trans: Oh, here is Dima calling right now!

examples.text: Мы же тебе говорили, она как барракуда!
examples.trans: We told you after all, she is like a barracuda!

meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (root 'явиться'). Used in Russian as an perfective verb focusing on a single completed action or result meaning 'to appear', forming an aspectual pair with 'появляться'.

examples.text: Как он появился, сразу стали пропадать продукты!
examples.trans: As soon as he appeared, groceries immediately started disappearing!

examples.text: Пусть только ещё раз здесь появится!
examples.trans: Let him just show up here one more time!

examples.text: У нас появилась хорошая идея.
examples.trans: We came up with a good idea.

meanings.note: Invariable Russian adverb used to modify verbs or whole clauses with the sense 'at once'.

examples.text: Сразу видно.
examples.trans: You can see it at once.

examples.text: Я сразу понял.
examples.trans: I understood at once.

examples.text: Вот, сразу видно, деловая женщина.
examples.trans: Now there's a businesswoman, you can see it at once.

meanings.note: Declinable feminine noun meaning 'steel', changing its case ending across all six Russian grammatical cases to mark its role in the clause.

examples.text: Это лучшая прочная сталь для кухни!
examples.trans: This is the best strong steel for the kitchen!

examples.text: Его сделали мастера из твёрдой стали.
examples.trans: Craftsmen made it from hard steel.

meanings.note: Prefix 'про-' indicates movement through, completion, or missing the mark (root 'падать'). Used in Russian as an perfective verb focusing on a single completed action or result meaning 'to immediately'.

examples.text: Как он появился, сразу стали пропадать продукты!
examples.trans: As soon as he appeared, groceries immediately started disappearing!

examples.text: Да, у нас пропадают свежие устрицы.
examples.trans: Yes, fresh oysters are going to waste here.

meanings.note: Declinable masculine noun meaning 'product', changing its case ending across all six Russian grammatical cases to mark its role in the clause.

examples.text: Как он появился, сразу стали пропадать продукты!

examples.trans: I was watching so that you would not steal groceries!

meanings.note: Everyday conversational Russian interj meaning 'thank you', frequent in spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Спасибо большое, друзья, мне очень приятно.
examples.trans: Thank you very much, friends, I am very pleased.

examples.text: Спасибо, дорогая, вы вечером точно будете?
examples.trans: Thank you, dear, will you definitely be there tonight?

examples.text: Спасибо, Сеня, я за ним прослежу.
examples.trans: Thank you, Senya, I will keep an eye on him.

meanings.note: Prefix 'про-' indicates movement through, completion, or missing the mark (root 'следить'). Used in Russian as an perfective verb focusing on a single completed action or result meaning 'to see to it', forming an aspectual pair with 'следить'.

examples.text: Спасибо, Сеня, я за ним прослежу.

examples.text: Я прослежу за детьми.
examples.trans: I'll keep an eye on the children.
